parties: BASF SE (acquirer) v. BASF India Limited (target); public minority shareholders
headline: BASF SE acquires remaining stake in BASF India via NCLT-convened delisting; shareholders approve scheme at 86.5% threshold
sum: BASF SE formally delists BASF India Limited following shareholder approval of a scheme to acquire the 14.8% public minority stake at ₹1,200 per equity share; NCLT-convened meeting held 24 June 2026 saw 86.5% of voting shareholding approve the delisting, consolidating the parent's 85.2% holding into a 100% subsidiary.
detail: BASF India Limited, a publicly listed subsidiary of Germany-domiciled BASF SE, initiated a delisting scheme under the NCLT framework after BASF SE decided to consolidate ownership. The parent held 85.2% pre-delisting; the scheme sought to acquire the remaining 14.8% public shares at ₹1,200 per share. The NCLT convened an equity shareholders' meeting on 24 June 2026, at which 86.5% of voting shareholding approved the scheme-exceeding the 75% threshold required under the Companies Act. Subsequent to approval, the delisting will remove BASF India from the BSE and NSE registers, converting it into a wholly-owned subsidiary.
